title: Termination of Insurer Program Agreements
content:
Either party may terminate an agreement under the Insurer Program Agreements by notice; the termination date is the tier's termination notice period in calendar days after the notice date. The notice period has run its full length. A proposed agreement may be withdrawn at any time before it takes effect (withdrawn proposal). Repair orders opened before the termination date finish under the agreement's terms; repair orders opened later are handled as for an insurer without an agreement.

## The notice period

The condition for recording a termination is that **the notice period has run its full length**. It is read from the termination notice date on that same agreement's record. The termination date, the agreement's last day in effect, falls the tier's notice period in calendar days after the notice date; the notice period has run its full length on the termination date and on any later day, and has not on any earlier day.

| Hypothetical notice date | Notice period | Termination date | Day before the termination date | On the termination date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 January 2026 | 60 days | 11 March 2026 | 10 March: not run its full length | 11 March: run its full length |
| 10 January 2026 | 30 days | 9 February 2026 | 8 February: not run its full length | 9 February: run its full length |

## What a termination records

A termination records the date notice was given, the termination date as the last day in effect, and one of four reasons: insurer notice, network notice, performance, or withdrawn proposal. The agreement's status becomes terminated. A proposed agreement withdrawn before it takes effect, and an active, under review or suspended agreement whose notice period ends, each move to terminated.

## Repair orders around the termination date

| Repair order opened | Handled |
|---|---|
| Before the termination date | Finishes under the agreement's terms |
| Later than the termination date | As for an insurer without an agreement |

## Basis questions

**Which party may give notice?** Either party, the insurer or the network.

**Does a proposed agreement need a notice period to be withdrawn?** A proposed agreement may be withdrawn at any time before it takes effect.
